verdict_text: NO. The second task vector is taken against an already-modified base, which is exactly the ordering hazard the specification calls out. The `add_` of `tv1` into `base::h.\1.\2` happens before `tv2` is computed, so the later `subtract_` yields `tv2 = ft2 - (base + 0.4*(ft1-base))` instead of `ft2 - base`; the output is `base + 0.4*(ft1-base) + 0.4*(ft2-base) - 0.16*(ft1-base)`, violating the formula in "Required result" step 2 (and the merged tensors will exceed the 1e-5 Frobenius tolerance). Fixing it requires computing both task vectors before either is added, i.e. moving the `tv1` `add_` after the `tv2` `subtract_`. Secondarily, the step-1 name check is only a tensor count of 160 per checkpoint, not a verification that the three checkpoints have the same tensor names.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
